bracket: [Textbook answer-key error: the printed key gives \(\Delta U = 21\) kJ, dropping the sign. The question asks for the CHANGE in internal energy, which here is a DECREASE. With the chapter's own convention \(\Delta U = Q - W\) (eq. 4.3, \(W\) the work done BY the system): the system releases heat, so \(Q = -130\) kJ, and work is done ON it, so \(W = -109\) kJ, giving \(\Delta U = -130 - (-109) = -21\) kJ. The sign does not depend on which convention is used — reading it as \(\Delta U = Q + W_{\text{on}} = -130 + 109\) returns the same \(-21\) kJ. Physically the system loses 130 kJ and gains 109 kJ, so 21 kJ leaves it.]

[Textbook answer-key error: the printed key gives \(23^\circ\text{C}\); the correct cold-reservoir temperature is \(-23^\circ\text{C}\). Carnot efficiency uses ABSOLUTE temperature: \(T_H = 727^\circ\text{C} = 1000\) K, and \(\eta = 1 - T_C/T_H = 0.75\) gives \(T_C = 250\) K \(= -23^\circ\text{C}\). The key is self-refuting: \(+23^\circ\text{C} = 296\) K would make \(\eta = 1 - 296/1000 = 0.704\), not the 75% the question states.]
